title: Indie Brief, Saturday 17 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Saturday 17 October.

Screen Daily reports that European film and TV organisations have issued a joint statement criticising a proposed cut to the AgoraEU cultural fund. The funding would be reduced from eight point six billion euros to six billion euros, which organisations say would be devastating for the screen sector across Europe.

title: Indie Brief, Friday 16 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Friday 16 October.

Screen Daily reports that Tessa Ross has said even successful producers are struggling to raise funding. Speaking to an audience in Rome, she noted that having made a film that worked doesn't guarantee anyone will trust you to make another one. It's a sobering reminder of the current state of independent film financing.

title: Indie Brief, Saturday 10 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Saturday 10 October.

Ava DuVernay's documentary Fourteenth has premiered as the closing night film of the New York Film Festival. Screen Daily reports the film is a rousing exploration of the current attack on the rights of Black Americans, following her Oscar-nominated earlier work Thirteenth. Fourteenth will stream on Netflix from December.

title: Indie Brief, Friday 2 October
description:
Good morning, this is Indie Brief for Friday 2 October.

Pakistan has made history at the Academy Awards by selecting a documentary as its official entry for Best International Feature. Deadline reports that Mo Naqvi's Hanging By a Wire, a nonfiction action thriller about a major news event from 2023, is the first documentary Pakistan has ever chosen for this distinction.
